raw.assessment: The incumbent remains credible for simpler repeated work: both workers completed repeated three-compartment orders in seven to nine minutes (D2-O6), close to the target. However, the overall median was 11 minutes, five customers reported component problems, and only seven of ten observed users succeeded unaided (D2-O2–O4). Mixed batches contained every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Overlapping partition widths among first- and second-attempt insertions (D2-O5) limit a width-only explanation; slot dimensions and orientation remain unmeasured. Preassembly's possible checking benefit is a hypothesis, not demonstrated protection against omissions.

openings.claim: Layout switching may add selection and checking work that an order-specific parts staging step could reduce while retaining full assembly.
openings.delta: Test whether the incumbent can meet the time target through order preparation before changing its assembly policy.
openings.prediction: For the same target layout and color, orders following a different layout take longer in selection/checking; staging reduces that difference without increasing component errors.
openings.probe: Use existing parts and slips for matched repeated-layout and switched-layout trials, with and without bench staging. Counterbalance workers and order. Record selection, staging, insertion, checking and packing separately; include staging in total time and audit contents against each order.
assumptions: Trials fit spare capacity before the fixed delivery date; otherwise defer them.
Staging uses existing materials and preserves dimensions, assortment, removable partitions, counts and colors.

openings.claim: Does short-partition confusion persist when contents and insertion fit are verified and customers receive only their ordered-layout diagram?
openings.delta: Separate instruction ambiguity from incorrect contents or physical insertion difficulty; the reported partition problems do not identify a single cause.
openings.prediction: If diagram ambiguity contributes, verified kits with an order-specific diagram produce fewer short-partition placement questions than verified kits with the current three-layout diagram.
openings.probe: Randomize ten willing participants between diagrams using matched, verified kits. Record unaided ordered-layout completion, misplaced short partitions, questions and insertion retries. Treat results as directional; this sample cannot establish the pilot success rate.
assumptions: Existing board samples and diagrams suffice without delaying delivery.
Any adopted diagram change must keep initial and recurring costs within the stipulated caps; product specifications remain intact.

raw.assessment: Selection errors, layout confusion and mixed-order delays suggest a shared handoff hypothesis; the observations do not establish their causes. One integrated opening is offered, with cost and deadline feasibility unresolved.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: adapt a tool shadow board into a reusable order-specific kitting mat, then carry its partition-to-position mapping onto the existing order slip for customer setup. Keep workshop assembly initially so any gain comes from selection and handoff changes.
openings.delta: Parent mechanisms are occupancy-based completeness checking and position-based assembly guidance, crossed at a shared partition identifier. Together they could detect omissions while explaining the short partition's destination. Failed correspondence: tool boards have fixed inventories; these orders vary in count and color, and similar partitions may be indistinguishable by outline. Change the material assumption to interchangeable paper overlays on spare board, with quantity and orientation labels; check exterior color separately. Repurpose the existing order slip's order identity as the link between selected contents and ordered layout. Its presence is supplied; readable layout annotation is a new enabling dependency. Existing cutting templates supply candidate outlines, whose correspondence to actual parts must be checked before use.
openings.prediction: The linked pair should reduce selection/checking time and short-partition placement errors more than either aid alone, without increasing insertion time or changing the product.
openings.probe: Use up to 15 sample sets for counterbalanced worker trials of baseline, mat alone, slip alone and linked aids across layouts; time each activity and seed recoverable omissions or substitutions. Have ten participants attempt their ordered arrangement using paired slip conditions with order counterbalanced; treat results as exploratory. Before adoption, cost preparation and annotations against both caps and the fixed deadline. Then measure the 60-order pilot: at least 59 complete orders, median time at most eight minutes, and customer success against the 90% target.
assumptions: Preparation and annotation fit the spending and delivery limits.
Original parts, footprint, capacity, removable joints, accepted counts and colors are retained.

critiques.assumption: A shared partition mapping makes workshop completeness and customer guidance jointly more reliable.
critiques.limitation: A wrong overlay could populate mat and slip consistently, producing a complete-looking kit for the wrong arrangement. D2-O1 establishes count and color variation, but no observation establishes this mapping failure. Z2 verifies contents without establishing affordable operational verification.
critiques.opening: Reconcile the shared mapping against the accepted order independently before using it for both staging and instructions.
critiques.comparison: Z1 organizes selection; Z2 clarifies destination; A1 links occupancy checking and destination guidance. Their interaction can propagate incorrect mappings. Reconciliation could intercept those errors but adds time and requires an authoritative order description.
critiques.probe: Proposed, unperformed: introduce recoverable wrong-layout overlays and examine whether ordinary A1 checking versus independent reconciliation catches them. Seeded results establish detection capability only, not natural error frequency.

openings.claim: Combine A1 linked aids with a separate accepted-order reconciliation before kit release.
openings.delta: Distinguish agreement between aids from correctness against the customer order; do not derive the independent check from the same overlay.
openings.prediction: Relative to mat alone, the slip should reduce destination confusion; relative to slip alone, the mat should improve omission detection. Relative to A1, reconciliation should catch more shared mapping errors. No time advantage is assumed.
openings.probe: Proposed, unperformed: smallest capability is independently recovering ordered layout, count and color and detecting a mismatched overlay. If feasible, reuse at most 15 sample sets across mat-only, slip-only, linked and reconciled-linked conditions; counterbalance workers. Include all preparation and checking in assembly/packing time. Use ten participants for exploratory first-use comparisons; assess original success thresholds in the 60-order pilot.
openings.fit: Preserves footprint, assortment, removable partitions, accepted counts and colors. Adoption remains conditional on both cost caps, fixed delivery date and the original performance targets.
assumptions: Accepted-order information independently specifies the intended arrangement.
Reconciliation does not merely repeat the overlay error.
Preparation and checking fit available working time; insertion difficulties remain unresolved.
